title: Model Entry Guard: automated license & restricted-weight vetting for onboarding
creator: Ava Kim
description:
Problem: As we expand Redwood's open-model catalog and support customer-supplied weights, we need an automated and auditable gating mechanism to prevent models with incompatible licenses or restricted distribution terms from being published. Without this, customers or internal teams may inadvertently expose non-distributable weights, violate third-party license terms, or ship models that trigger export/regulatory restrictions.

Goals:
- Automatically detect license metadata and classify licenses into allow/conditional/deny buckets.
- Validate model weight provenance (hashes, signatures, distribution rights) and flag restricted or unknown provenance.
- Integrate a human-in-the-loop workflow for gray-area licenses or provenance gaps, including legal/SSO approvals and an auditable decision record.
- Prevent publishing of performance profiles or version pinning until checks pass.
- Surface flagged models in the Console (model catalog) and provide clear remediation steps to contributors.

Scope: Public onboarding flow for new models and a verification step when uploading new model versions. This covers both curated open models and customer-supplied weights (Private/Dedicated flows). Does not include runtime policy enforcement for inference-time prompts (handled elsewhere).
acceptance_criteria:
1) The onboarding API refuses to transition a model to 'Published' or allow version pinning if license is in deny bucket or provenance is missing.
2) A searchable audit trail exists recording license scan results, hash/signature validation, reviewer decisions, and timestamps.
3) Gray cases automatically create a 'legal review' task and notify the reviewer group; models stay in Holding state until manual approval.
4) Console shows an explicit 'License: <license name or unknown>' field with a one-click link to the audit record and remediation steps.
5) Integration tests exercise at least three license types (permissive, non-commercial, no-derivatives) and a bad-provenance case.
6) Dependencies ENG-1984 (SPDX scanner) and ENG-2057 (provenance & signature service) merged and available in staging.
tasks: Define allow/conditional/deny license taxonomy with Legal — create SPDX mapping and a small white/gray/blacklist
Spec: onboarding API contract changes (new "checks" status + error codes) — PM -> ENG handoff
ENG: Integrate SPDX license scanner (ENG-1984) and return normalized ID and risk level
ENG: Wire provenance verification service (ENG-2057) to compute model weight hashes, verify signatures, and surface trust flags
UX: Console UI for Holding state, audit view, and reviewer action buttons
Legal: Draft escalation & approval playbook for conditional licenses and export control flags
E2E tests & CI: gating behavior for publish / version-pin / profile-publish
Monitoring: dashboard for flagged models, weekly digest to Legal & Catalog owners
decisions: Use SPDX identifiers as canonical license IDs for scans (avoids free-text parsing)
Three-tier license policy: allow (auto-pass), conditional (requires human review), deny (auto-block)
Provenance verification must include both manifest-level metadata and weight hash/signature verification; missing signature -> conditional
Model performance profiles and version pin actions will be blocked until the model passes compliance checks
Owners can request an override only via documented legal approval flow; override creates an auditable exception record
